input.strategy_title: Experiment comparison for training and pipeline runs
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Data scientists iterate across dozens of training and pipeline runs but have no
way to compare them inside the platform: parameters and metrics live in
per-run pages, so comparison happens in exported spreadsheets. Model promotion
decisions need side-by-side visibility into what changed between candidate
runs and how their metrics differ. (Requirements below were consolidated from
two customer councils; some overlap in wording was kept from the sources.)

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Registered model versions link back to the run that produced them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Provide a run "diff" view that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs list and the registry. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Model Registry
- Data Science Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automatic best-run selection or promotion
- Comparison across clusters or across projects

## Open Questions

None.

# Run comparison view in the Dashboard

## Description

Deliver a run comparison capability in the Dashboard: users can select two or more training or pipeline runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side, with a diff presentation that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs. This gives data scientists in-platform visibility into what changed between candidate runs, replacing comparison via exported spreadsheets and supporting model promotion decisions.

## Scope

- Multi-select of two or more runs from the runs list in the Dashboard.
- Side-by-side view of the selected runs' parameters and metrics.
- Diff presentation between two selected runs, highlighting which parameters and metrics differ (added, removed, or changed values).
- Comparison covers both training runs and Data Science Pipelines runs, reading run parameters and metrics through the interfaces the Dashboard already uses to surface runs.
- Comparison is an additional view: no changes to run execution, run storage, or the existing behavior of the run list and run detail pages.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a list of runs, when the user selects two or more runs, then the Dashboard offers a comparison action that opens a side-by-side view of those runs' parameters and metrics.
- Given a comparison of exactly two runs, then the view highlights which parameters and metrics differ between them.
- Given a selection that includes Data Science Pipelines runs, then their parameters and metrics are presented in the comparison the same as training runs (passive validation of the Data Science Pipelines component — no code change in that component).
- Given a selected run with missing parameters or metrics, then the comparison renders the missing values without breaking the view.
- The existing run list and run detail pages continue to function unchanged.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard.
- HLR-3 (P1, consolidated with HLR-1): a run diff view highlighting which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs — a presentation mode of the same comparison surface over the same run data, delivered in this epic.

# Link registered model versions to their producing runs

## Description

Record, on each registered model version, a link back to the run that produced it, so that downstream consumers (including the Dashboard's registry UI) can resolve the producing run and open a comparison from the Model Registry. This establishes the training-lineage connection the registry's role calls for.

## Scope

- When a model version is registered from a run, store the identity of the producing run on the model version, using the Model Registry's existing model-version metadata extension point (custom properties on ModelVersion entities).
- Expose the producing-run link through the registry's existing API surface so clients can resolve it.
- Backward compatibility: existing model versions without a producing-run link remain valid and are served unchanged.
- No changes to model serving, registration workflow semantics, or the registry's storage model beyond the added metadata.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a model version registered from a run, then the model version carries a resolvable link to the run that produced it.
- Given a client reading a model version through the registry's API, then the producing-run link is returned when present.
- Given an existing model version with no producing-run link, then it remains valid and is served unchanged.
- Given two model versions produced by different runs, then each carries its own correct link with no cross-contamination.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1, registry side): registered model versions link back to the run that produced them.

# Open run comparison from the Model Registry UI

## Description

Add an entry point in the Dashboard's Model Registry UI so a user can open a run comparison for the run linked to a registered model version. This connects the registry's producing-run links to the run comparison capability, letting data scientists make model promotion decisions with side-by-side visibility directly from the registry context.

## Scope

- In the Dashboard's registered model version view, surface the producing-run link recorded in the Model Registry and offer an action to open a comparison that includes the producing run.
- The comparison opened from the registry presents the same side-by-side and diff capability as the comparison opened from the runs list.
- Graceful degradation when a model version has no producing-run link: the action is hidden or disabled with no user-facing error.
- In-project scope only: comparison across clusters or projects remains out of scope, per the strategy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a registered model version that carries a producing-run link, when the user views it in the Dashboard's registry UI, then an action is available to open a comparison that includes the producing run.
- Given a comparison opened from the registry, then it presents parameters and metrics side by side with diff highlighting between two selected runs, matching the comparison opened from the runs list.
- Given a model version without a producing-run link, then the registry view degrades gracefully with no user-facing error.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1, Dashboard side): a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry.
